summary.headline: Balrampur Chini raises PLA project cost by INR230 crore to INR3,080 crore and approves INR450 crore preferential equity plus INR200 crore debentures.
summary.overview: The company held a post-board-meeting call (board met 23 April 2026) on the PLA project, its cost overrun, and financing. PLA project cost rises to INR3,080 crore from INR2,850 crore, attributed to construction materials, supply chain, forex, and engineering refinements. Board approved a lactogypsum-to-gypsum-board plant at Kumbhi (INR160 crore, ~76 lakh boards per annum, commercial production in 18 months). Financing includes a preferential equity issue of about INR450 crore at INR483 per share, with promoters subscribing about INR193 crore to keep family stake at 43%, plus an enabling resolution for INR200 crore debentures. Quarterly business performance was not discussed given the silent period.

financial_highlights.change: up INR230 crore from INR2,850 crore

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR450 crore at INR483 per share

segments.name: PLA (polylactic acid) project
segments.commentary: Project cost raised to INR3,080 crore from INR2,850 crore; commissioning reiterated for Q3 (management said feasible but tough). Machinery expected to arrive soon; UP bioplastic policy 50% capital subsidy said to apply to revised cost.

segments.name: Lactogypsum to gypsum board plant (Kumbhi)
segments.commentary: INR160 crore plant, ~76 lakh boards per annum capacity, commercial production in 18 months. PLA at 80,000 tonnes yields ~1.16-1.2 lakh tonnes lactogypsum, ~63 lakh boards; revenue potential ~INR150 crore per year; target market UP and North India initially.

segments.name: Auxilo (NBFC stake)
segments.commentary: Management said it would eventually offload some or all of its NBFC stake to delever; no timeline or valuation given. Last dilution implied Auxilo market cap of about INR3,000-3,200 crore.

guidance_outlook: PLA project cost of INR3,080 crore described as final revision, with machinery arrival expected soon.
PLA commissioning on track for Q3 FY27 per CFO; Chairman called it a tough but feasible target.
Gypsum board plant commercial production expected in about 18 months; marketing and channel decisions deferred to 3-6 months after plant setup.
Preferential proceeds to fund PLA (INR230 crore) and lactogypsum plant (INR160 crore), with balance for general corporate purposes; sugar season cane purchases also cited as a use of liquidity.
capex_capacity: PLA project cost INR3,080 crore (from INR2,850 crore); overrun attributed to construction materials, supply chain, forex (EUR moved from 90 to 110), freight costs, and engineering changes.
Lactogypsum processing plant at Kumbhi: INR160 crore outlay, ~76 lakh boards per annum capacity, 18-month timeline.
Raw material for gypsum boards is lactogypsum from own PLA output; steam and power from the PLA plant's boiler to be transfer-priced as cost to board plant and revenue to PLA.
Management said the Euro-denominated machinery cost increase and freight (one consignment cost INR9 crore to transport; shipping routing affected by Hormuz and Cape of Good Hope) drove overruns.
demand_pricing: Board prices factored into the gypsum board business case have risen about 25% since evaluation began due to the West Asia crisis, per Chairman; described as a recent development.
Management said existing gypsum disposal options (cement plants) offer limited interest, very poor pricing and limited off-take, motivating the conversion.
Sales route not finalised: options under evaluation, including outsourcing to an established brand (e.g., Gyproc) versus own brand; management said it does not want large branding spend.
Board is positioning boards on eco-friendly, no-mining attributes; no bio-based or recycled-content premium envisaged currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity so close to the commercial timeline when financing is tied up and leverage is moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman cited a roughly 5% dilution with promoters participating; aim is to maintain credit rating, avoid ratio breaches as the company borrows at about 6.75%, and fund INR390 crore (INR230 crore plus INR160 crore) plus sugar-season cane purchases.

qa_highlights.question: Lactogypsum output, revenue and margin of the gypsum board plant?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: 80,000 tonnes PLA gives ~1.16-1.2 lakh tonnes lactogypsum, ~63 lakh boards, revenue ~INR150 crore per year, payback about 5 years; Chairman said payback may shorten with higher board prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will the NBFC stake be sold to delever?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said yes, eventually (100%), but timing and valuation not disclosed; referenced prior Auxilo dilution at INR3,000-3,200 crore market cap.

qa_highlights.question: Does the cost overrun alter plant yield or efficiency, and is the revised cost final?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said minor engineering tweaks may affect details but cannot be quantified now; said the revision should be final as machinery is arriving soon. Attributed about 90% of overrun to genuine costs, 10% to supplier price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is the UP bioplastic policy 50% capital subsidy applicable to the revised cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the policy document does not curtail investment, so the revised cost should be eligible.

qa_highlights.question: Use of the INR450 crore preferential proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said INR230 crore for PLA and INR160 crore for lactogypsum plant; balance for general corporate purposes.

risks_watch: Further cost escalation on PLA (forex, freight, supplier pricing) despite management calling the INR3,080 crore figure final.
Q3 FY27 PLA commissioning timeline; management described it as tough.
Gypsum board economics depend on board price (up ~25%) and an unfinalised sales/distribution route; 5-year payback is management's estimate.
Auxilo NBFC stake sale: timing and valuation not defined.
Dilution of about 5% and related-party promoter subscription; shareholder reaction to the equity raise.
Management tone on some questions was evasive (Auxilo timing, sales route, ethanol economics deferred offline).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic rationale and PLA commissioning, but defensive on the equity raise timing and cost overrun, and deferred several questions (Auxilo valuation, sales channel, branding, ethanol economics) to later or offline.
key_quotes: The proposed plant has an investment outlay of INR160 crore and is expected to have a production capacity of ~76 lakh boards per annum, with commercial production starting in 18 months.
So if you see, we have put in 43% of INR450 crore, which is about INR193 crore, which is exactly synergistic with our existing stake.
We want to avoid any speculation or uneven access to information , no one should have a preferential understanding.
